sentences.text: Before writing a single line of model code, it pays to have a clear map of the territory: what are the exact numbers that define a GPT-2 model, and which training knobs will we be turning throughout this book?
sentences.reason: Introductory framing question with no factual claim.

sentences.text: This chapter answers both questions.
sentences.reason: Connective tissue describing chapter purpose.

sentences.text: Think of it as a reference you can flip back to whenever you need to double-check a dimension, a layer count, or a learning rate.
sentences.reason: Framing statement about chapter usage.

sentences.text: GPT-2 was released in four sizes.
sentences.reason: Factual claim about GPT-2 release with no citation. Not contradicted by claims but not explicitly supported either.

sentences.text: Each size shares the same fundamental architecture—transformer blocks stacked on top of a token embedding layer—but differs in how wide and how deep that stack is.
sentences.reason: Descriptive statement about architectural similarities and differences; no specific factual claim requiring citation.

sentences.text: Understanding the relationship between these sizes gives you intuition for how scaling works in practice.
sentences.reason: Pedagogical framing with no factual claim.

sentences.text: The smallest member of the family is **GPT-2 small**, which has 124 million parameters [c2841].
sentences.reason: Claim c2841 directly states GPT-2 small model has 124 million parameters.

sentences.text: It uses an embedding dimension of 768, 12 transformer layers, and 12 attention heads [c3536].
sentences.reason: Claim c3536 states GPT-2 small (124M) has embedding dimension 768, 12 layers, and 12 attention heads.

sentences.text: Its context length—the maximum number of tokens the model can attend to at once—is 1024 [c3490].
sentences.reason: Claim c3490 states GPT-2 small model context length is 1024.

sentences.text: This is the model we will build from scratch in the early chapters of this book, and the hyperparameter values shown throughout those chapters correspond to this configuration [c3496].
sentences.reason: Pedagogical statement about which model will be built; c3496 supports that the values shown are for the 124M model.

sentences.text: Moving up in scale, **GPT-2 medium** has 345 million parameters [c3434] (sometimes cited as 355 million [c1748, c3537]).
sentences.reason: Claim c3434 states GPT-2 Medium has 345 million parameters. Claims c1748 and c3537 both reference 355 million, supporting the parenthetical note about alternative citations.

sentences.text: It widens and deepens the architecture considerably: the embedding dimension grows to 1024, the number of layers doubles to 24, and the number of attention heads increases to 16 [c3537].
sentences.reason: Claim c3537 states GPT-2 medium (355M) has embedding dimension 1024, 24 layers, and 16 attention heads.

sentences.text: Its context size remains 1024 tokens [c1737].
sentences.reason: Claim c1737 states GPT-2 medium has a context size of 1024 tokens.

sentences.text: As a general pattern, as GPT-2 model complexity increases, the number of transformer blocks also increases [c3499].
sentences.reason: Claim c3499 directly states this pattern.

sentences.text: **GPT-2 large** reaches 774 million parameters with an embedding dimension of 1280, 36 layers, and 20 attention heads [c3538].
sentences.reason: Claim c3538 states GPT-2 large (774M) has embedding dimension 1280, 36 layers, and 20 attention heads.

sentences.text: Finally, **GPT-2 XL** tops out at 1558 million parameters, using an embedding dimension of 1600, 48 layers, and 25 attention heads [c3539].
sentences.reason: Claim c3539 states GPT-2 XL (1558M) has embedding dimension 1600, 48 layers, and 25 attention heads.

sentences.text: Throughout this book we represent a model's configuration as a plain Python dictionary.
sentences.reason: Pedagogical statement about representation choice.

sentences.text: Here is the canonical configuration for GPT-2 small (124M) that we will use as our starting point:
sentences.reason: Introductory statement before code block.

sentences.text:
GPT_CONFIG_124M = {
    "vocab_size": 50257,           # Vocabulary size
    "context_length": 1024,        # Context length
    "emb_dim": 768,                # Embedding dimension
    "n_heads": 12,                 # Number of attention heads
    "n_layers": 12,                # Number of layers
    "drop_rate": 0.1,              # Dropout rate
    "qkv_bias": False              # Query-Key-Value bias
}
sentences.reason: Claim c438 contains the exact code block with all matching values.

sentences.text: Every key in this dictionary corresponds to a meaningful architectural choice.
sentences.reason: Framing statement about the configuration dictionary.

sentences.text: We will walk through each one in turn.
sentences.reason: Transition statement.

sentences.text: The vocabulary size is 50257 tokens [c526, c529].
sentences.reason: Both c526 and c529 state that GPT-2 has a vocabulary size of 50257 tokens.

sentences.text: This is the number of unique tokens that the model's embedding layer must handle—one learned vector per token.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about what vocabulary size means; no factual claim requiring citation.

sentences.text: Intuitively, this is the size of the model's "alphabet," and every input token ID must fall within the range `[0, vocab_size - 1]`.
sentences.reason: Intuitive explanation with no factual claim requiring citation.

sentences.text: The context length is 1024 for the full GPT-2 small model [c3490].
sentences.reason: Claim c3490 states GPT-2 small model context length is 1024.

sentences.text: This is the maximum sequence length the model can process in a single forward pass; tokens beyond this limit simply cannot be attended to.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about what context length means.

sentences.text: The full specification of a GPT model configuration requires this value to be set explicitly [c3847].
sentences.reason: Claim c3847 states that the GPT model configuration requires specification of context length.

sentences.text: For the hands-on tutorials in this book, we reduce the context length to 256 tokens [c537, c1671].
sentences.reason: Both c537 and c1671 state that context length is reduced to 256 tokens for the tutorial.

sentences.text: This reduction is deliberate: it cuts memory and compute requirements enough that the training examples can run on a laptop [c537].
sentences.reason: Claim c537 states the reduction is to reduce computational resource requirements and allow execution on laptops.

sentences.text: Functionally the model is identical; only the maximum sequence length changes [c494].
sentences.reason: Claim c494 states that a context length of 256 tokens is used instead of 1024 for computational efficiency in the tutorial, implying functional equivalence.

sentences.text: The embedding dimension is 768 [c531, c1673].
sentences.reason: Both c531 and c1673 state that embedding dimension is 768.

sentences.text: This is the size of the vector space into which each token ID is projected; for GPT-2 small, every token is represented as a 768-dimensional vector [c3492].
sentences.reason: Claim c3492 states that for GPT-2 small, each token is represented as a 768-dimensional vector.

sentences.text: The same dimensionality flows through every subsequent layer—attention, feed-forward, and layer normalization—so this single number has a large influence on the model's total parameter count.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about architectural implications; no specific factual claim requiring citation.

sentences.text: `n_heads` is the number of attention heads present in each transformer block [c3494].
sentences.reason: Claim c3494 defines n_heads as the number of attention heads present in each transformer block.

sentences.text: For GPT-2 small this is 12 [c532, c1674].
sentences.reason: Both c532 and c1674 state that number of attention heads is 12.

sentences.text: Multi-head attention splits the embedding dimension across heads, so each head operates on a $768 / 12 = 64$-dimensional subspace.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about how multi-head attention works; the arithmetic is a straightforward consequence of stated values.

sentences.text: Intuitively, different heads can learn to attend to different kinds of relationships in the input simultaneously.
sentences.reason: Intuitive explanation with no factual claim requiring citation.

sentences.text: `n_layers` is the number of transformer blocks stacked in the model [c3495].
sentences.reason: Claim c3495 defines n_layers as the number of transformer blocks in the model.

sentences.text: GPT-2 small uses 12 [c533, c888, c1675].
sentences.reason: All three claims state that GPT-2 small uses 12 transformer blocks/layers.

sentences.text: Each block contains its own multi-head self-attention sublayer and feed-forward sublayer, so doubling `n_layers` roughly doubles the depth—and a significant portion of the parameter count—of the network.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about architectural implications; no specific factual claim requiring citation.

sentences.text: The dropout rate is 0.1 in the standard GPT-2 small configuration [c534, c1676].
sentences.reason: Both c534 and c1676 state that dropout rate is 0.1.

sentences.text: Dropout is a regularization technique; setting it to 0.1 means that during training, 10% of activations are randomly zeroed out at each dropout layer.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about what dropout does; standard technical knowledge.

sentences.text: When experimenting or debugging, it is common to set this to zero [c498], which disables regularization and makes the forward pass fully deterministic.
sentences.reason: Claim c498 states that dropout rate can be set to zero and is a regularization parameter.

sentences.text: The query, key, and value weight matrices are initialized without bias terms—`qkv_bias` is `False` [c499, c535, c1677].
sentences.reason: All three claims state that query, key, and value bias is set to false or that these matrices are initialized without bias terms.

sentences.text: This is a deliberate design decision that matches the original GPT-2 implementation.
sentences.reason: Contextual statement about design choice; no specific factual claim requiring citation.

sentences.text: Omitting these biases slightly reduces the parameter count and has been found to work well in practice.
sentences.reason: General statement about practical implications; no specific factual claim requiring citation.

sentences.text: It is worth noting that not all GPT-2 configurations use exactly the same defaults.
sentences.reason: Transition statement introducing variation across configurations.

sentences.text: When loading pretrained GPT-2 weights (as opposed to training from scratch), the base configuration sets the dropout rate to 0.0 [c1741] and sets `qkv_bias` to `True` [c1742].
sentences.reason: Claim c1741 states GPT-2 base configuration uses dropout rate of 0.0. Claim c1742 states GPT-2 base configuration sets query-key-value bias to true.

sentences.text: These differences matter when you are trying to match a pretrained checkpoint exactly.
sentences.reason: Contextual statement about practical implications.

sentences.text: For instruction fine-tuning experiments later in the book, GPT-2 medium (355M) is preferred over the 124M model because the smaller model does not perform well on instruction-following tasks [c1748].
sentences.reason: Claim c1748 states that GPT-2 medium (355M) is chosen instead of the smaller 124M model because the smaller model does not perform well in instruction fine-tuning tasks.
